objective: Use Step-3 item-level seller-facing identity signals to mine high-precision Step-5 positive candidates without treating Step-11 predictions as labels.

target_queue_size.note: This is not a quota. If seller-facing direct identity evidence is exhausted, leave the queue small rather than dilute it with soft semantic candidates.

positive: Use positive only when both sides expose the same seller-facing direct identifier, such as Telegram/Wickr/Wechat/Jabber/QQ/Bat/phone/wallet/PGP.
Email is positive only when it is clearly seller-facing contact, not a leaked account, sample credential, or customer/victim data field.
A shared external URL remains support-only unless there is separate seller-facing direct contact evidence.
uncertain: Use uncertain for product/victim-data ambiguity, one-sided context weakness, or shared identifiers embedded inside sample data.
Use uncertain when a parser hit is plausible but cannot survive paper-level identity-proof scrutiny.
negative: Use negative only for clear parser noise or evidence that the sellers are controller-distinct.
Do not mark negative merely because products differ.

hard_rules: Step-3 item-level identity signals are extraction evidence only; they do not create labels by themselves.
Do not use Step-11 cluster membership or model score as a positive label.
Do not auto-promote product/victim-data emails, public URLs, high-frequency generic handles, or parser fragments.
If the queue cannot produce enough defensible positives, report direct-identity evidence scarcity instead of forcing few-shot improvement claims.
After any reviewed labels are applied, rerun Step 5 freeze and then rerun Step 7/9/11 from the refreshed boundary.
